caption: Define the work → Plan delivery → Keep the record. A planning map for the HiBAR journal: follow the guides from defining work to retaining the project record.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: define the work — understand product and project scope; plan delivery — coordinate access and documentation; keep the record — capture inspection and handover.

alt: HiBAR planning diagram: define the work — understand product and project scope; plan delivery — coordinate access and documentation; keep the record — capture inspection and handover.

caption: Define the work → Plan delivery → Keep the record. A planning map for the HiBAR journal: follow the guides from defining work to retaining the project record.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: define the work — understand product and project scope; plan delivery — coordinate access and documentation; keep the record — capture inspection and handover.

photograph.caption: HiBAR applied to an exposed roof deck and joists, as pictured by its manufacturer. The guides below cover product identification, scope, access, inspections and handover for project planning.

caption: Scope map → Design reference → Associated work. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: scope map — mark areas included and excluded; design reference — link each area to its assembly; associated work — record access and preparation.

caption: Product → Assembly → Project. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: product — confirm hibar material identity; assembly — match the specified building system; project — check the applicable design records.

photograph.caption: SOPREMA’s HiBAR product photograph shows a coated roof deck and exposed joists. It identifies the material in context; the project’s specified assembly and inspection records establish the required performance.

caption: Same design → Same inclusions → Clear differences. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: same design — compare a shared scope and assembly; same inclusions — align access and preparation; clear differences — record exclusions before award.

caption: Storage → Delivery → Work area. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: storage — agree the protected storage area; delivery — record labels and received condition; work area — link material records to location.

caption: Locate damage → Review repair → Close record. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: locate damage — record the affected area and stage; review repair — confirm the approved repair method; close record — retain review and inspection results.

caption: Survey → Find the cause → Compare options. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: survey — map visible and adjacent conditions; find the cause — review why the damage occurred; compare options — scope repair and replacement fully.

caption: Structural coating → Service routes → Penetrations. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: structural coating — define the treated building element; service routes — coordinate pipes and cable access; penetrations — identify separate firestop requirements.

photograph.caption: The HiBAR-coated roof deck and joists in this manufacturer image illustrate the overhead elements that must be coordinated with service routes. The image does not establish a penetration’s firestop requirements.

caption: Occupied space → Work zone → Reopening. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: occupied space — record users and essential access; work zone — review separation and work sequence; reopening — agree who accepts the completed area.

caption: Visual brief → Finish review → Separate approvals. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: visual brief — describe the intended appearance; finish review — check proposed changes with suppliers; separate approvals — keep appearance and compliance distinct.

photograph.caption: The manufacturer’s HiBAR photograph shows the textured appearance across a roof deck and joists. Use an agreed project sample to review the intended finish; this photograph does not promise an identical colour or texture.

caption: Project references → Product documents → Review record. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: project references — collect current drawings and revisions; product documents — attach current supporting documents; review record — track comments and acceptance status.

caption: Design requirement → Inspection access → Traceable result. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: design requirement — identify project-specific criteria; inspection access — plan when and where checks occur; traceable result — record location and inspection outcome.

caption: Existing surface → Preparation → Review point. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: existing surface — record material and surface condition; preparation — confirm required preparation steps; review point — check readiness before application.

photograph.caption: This HiBAR reference photograph shows the completed coating over overhead building elements. A substrate review concerns the surface beneath that coating, which cannot be assessed from the finished photograph.

caption: Equipment route → Overhead space → Work sequence. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: equipment route — map entry and movement clearances; overhead space — show services and obstructions; work sequence — coordinate access with other trades.

caption: Building + objective → Evidence → Requested response. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: building + objective — explain location and project purpose; evidence — attach drawings and labelled photos; requested response — ask for scope and availability review.

caption: Installed scope → Inspection closeout → Future work. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: installed scope — retain final locations and revisions; inspection closeout — resolve and record outstanding items; future work — keep documents available for repairs.

caption: Overview → Detail + label → Written evidence. This diagram explains the review sequence covered on this page.
alt: HiBAR planning diagram: overview — show the area and project stage; detail + label — retain original files and clear labels; written evidence — connect images to project records.
